Do judges' leniency rankings hold? Monotonicity checks

Source: R/jdgiv.R
jmono.Rd

The decision rate of each judge (with a chi-square test that the rate is the same for all, and its range), and two checks of the monotonicity a judge-leniency design rests on.

Usage

jmono(
  judge,
  d,
  y = NULL,
  grp = NULL,
  w = NULL,
  lo = NULL,
  hi = NULL,
  minn = 30,
  adj = "holm",
  alpha = 0.05
)

Arguments

judge

The judge of each case: labels.

d

The decision of each case: 0 or 1 (or FALSE, TRUE).

y

NULL, or the outcome of each case: numbers.

grp

NULL, or the group of each case: labels.

w

NULL, or a weight from 0 for each case (for the rates and outcome means; the tests use the counts).

lo, hi

NULL (the smallest and largest outcome) or the bounds of the outcome.

minn

The fewest cases a judge needs in a group to be compared there: one number from 0.

adj

The adjustment of the p-values: "none", "bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "BH" or "BY".

alpha

The level at which an adjusted p-value marks a reversal as significant.

Value

An object of class jmono, a list: judges (judge, n, rate, with y outcome; most lenient first); homog (chisq, df, p, min, max); slope, with y, one row per pair (j the more lenient, k, dp, dy, bound, viol, late); sub, with grp, a list of pairs (group, stricter, lenient, their overall rates rates, ratel, their group rates grates, gratel, their cases ns, nl, z, p, padj, reversed, signif), summary (pairs, reversed, share, signif, refuted the pairs significantly reversed, judges in them) and slopes (group, judges, cases, slope); and alpha. The pairs grow as the square of the judges.

Details

  • With outcomes y in [lo, hi]: if judges are nested (a stricter judge detains everyone a more lenient one detains), the outcome means of two judges differ by at most (hi - lo) times the difference in their rates. Every pair is checked; a violation refutes the nesting of that pair. The ratio late is the effect on the marginal cases between them.

  • With groups of cases grp: nested judges are ordered the same way in every group. For each pair of judges with at least minn cases in a group, the stricter judge overall should not be more lenient there; z is the pooled two-proportion statistic of the lenient judge's group rate over the stricter's, its one-sided p-value is adjusted over all comparisons, and slopes regresses each group's rates on the overall ones (Frandsen, Lefgren and Leslie 2023).

See proof("jmono").

References

Frandsen, B. R., Lefgren, L. J. and Leslie, E. C. (2023). Judging judge fixed effects. American Economic Review, 113(1), 253-277. doi:10.1257/aer.20201860

Examples

set.seed(9)
j <- sample(paste0("J", 1:6), 1200, TRUE)
len <- c(J1 = 0.2, J2 = 0.3, J3 = 0.35, J4 = 0.4, J5 = 0.5, J6 = 0.6)
d <- rbinom(1200, 1, len[j])
g <- sample(c("adult", "youth"), 1200, TRUE)
r <- jmono(j, d, grp = g)
r$sub$summary
#>       pairs    reversed       share      signif     refuted      judges 
#> 30.00000000  1.00000000  0.03333333  0.00000000  0.00000000  0.00000000
